title: Per-customer EU affinity, quarantine & override protocol for geo-routing
creator: Aisha Romero
description: Implement a per-customer routing affinity and quarantine mechanism that enforces EU-only routing constraints while allowing emergency operator overrides and safe fallback to compatible model variants. This ticket defines the protocol, runtime hooks, data-flow guarantees, and observability requirements needed to route requests based on tenant residency preferences, allowlist/denylist rules, and tier-based routing policies.
acceptance_criteria: Requests carrying tenant 'residency=europe' header are routed only to EU-designated hosts unless an explicit customer override is configured.

When EU-only routing cannot be satisfied (no capacity / circuit open), requests enter 'quarantine' mode: persisted to a retry queue with explanatory error and metric tagging; optionally fall back to a compatible EU-hosted model variant if available.
Operator override flow exists: a temporary override token can be applied to a tenant to allow non-EU routing for a bounded window with audit logs and TTL enforcement.
Allowlist/denylist rules are respected at policy-evaluation time and exposed in the Console for troubleshooting with clear provenance (who changed what and when).
New metrics emitted: tenant_eu_routing_attempts, tenant_eu_quarantine_rate, tenant_override_uses, fallback_variant_hits, routing_policy_eval_latency.
implementation_notes:
- Policy evaluation will run at the Routing Decision Service (RDS) layer. Implement a per-request policy envelope that includes tenant_id, residency_hint, customer_allowdeny_rules, and tier.
- Add a new enum route_outcome {ROUTED_EU, FALLBACK_VARIANT, QUARANTINED, OVERRIDDEN, DENIED} to tracing and logs.
- Quarantine storage: a short-lived SQS-style queue with visibility timeout and backoff. Include a small embedded retry worker in the edge plane to handle re-evaluation after capacity changes.
- Override tokens: signed JWT minted by Console with aud=router, exp within 24h, and scope="egress:non-eu". Routers must validate signature against platform key and log a structured audit entry with user id.
- Fallback model variant mapping: versioned JSON mapping maintained in model-catalog service and surfaced to RDS; fallback only permitted to variants with 'data_residency=EU' tag removed explicitly by admin.
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: Silent privacy violations if override is misused. Mitigation: Overrides require two-person approval in Console and automatic revocation after 24h; audit ship to SIEM.
Risk: Increased latency from policy eval. Mitigation: Cache policy decisions per-tenant for short TTL (30s) and measure policy_eval_latency; prefetch allow/deny lists for high-volume tenants.

Risk: Retry storms when quarantined queue backfills. Mitigation: Staggered exponential backoff and global circuit breaker per-tenant/backpressure signals to callers (429 with Retry-After and quarantine_reason).
Risk: Complexity interacting with Dedicated capacity routing. Mitigation: Add explicit capability flags on dedicated pools; policy evaluation must be aware of pool capability tags.
rollout_plan: 1) Feature-flag gating: default off. 2) Canary roll: enable for internal tenants (redwood-infra) for 48h. 3) Incremental enablement for selected customers with SLO monitoring. 4) After 2 weeks and no regressions, enable platform-wide. 5) Post-rollout: run a 30-day audit of override usage and quarantine events.
testing_plan: Unit tests for policy evaluation logic, integration tests covering allow/deny precedence, e2e tests with simulated capacity loss to validate quarantine behavior, chaos test to simulate override token expiry during request, and performance test to ensure <5ms median policy eval.
observability: Add dashboards and alerts: SLA: tenant_eu_quarantine_rate < 0.5% for paid customers; Alert when tenant_override_uses > 3 in 1h for a single tenant; Trace sampling for route_outcome!=ROUTED_EU at 100% for first week of canary.
